answer: One defense is anchored capability quotas: every agent identity must be rooted in a scarce, verifiable anchor, such as an attested device key or a reputable service account, and each anchor receives only a small kernel of voting and trading rights per epoch. Extra rights are earned through audited work, never claimed in bulk. A jade-level credential, awarded only after sustained honest service, unlocks higher limits. A sybil farmer can mint fake names, but each starts with the same tiny kernel and no anchor to scale it, so swaying a vote means buying or earning thousands of real anchors.
